長胴太鼓在江戶時代達到成熟，成為神社祭典、民間表演與戲劇活動的重要樂器。其深厚的: The nagado-daiko reached maturity in the Edo period and became an important instrument of shrine festivals, folk performance and theatrical events. Its deep low resonance and its crisp high register made it widely used in traditional performing arts such as nō and kabuki. In modern times it has become the core instrument of taiko performance art, carried around the world and turned into an important symbol of Japanese culture. Its distinctive timbre and impact have won it wide recognition and affection on the international music stage.
長胴太鼓屬於日本膜鳴樂器，在組太鼓（kumi-daiko）合奏中常以桶形鼓出現，: The nagado-daiko is a Japanese membranophone, appearing usually as the barrel drum in kumi-daiko ensembles alongside smaller drums such as the shime-daiko. Taiko are used at festivals, in religious rites, as theatre accompaniment and in concert performance; in traditional settings they also appear in kabuki, nōgaku, gagaku, kagura and Buddhist obon rites. In ensemble playing the drums are sometimes joined by voices, strings or winds.
長胴太鼓屬膜鳴樂器，以鼓棒敲擊鼓面發聲。來源所見早期形象顯示桶形鼓可懸於肩，在腰: The nagado-daiko is a membranophone, sounding when the drumhead is struck with a stick. The early images seen in the source show a barrel drum that could be slung from the shoulder and struck with sticks at hip height; modern ensembles also pay attention to rhythm, posture, grip, costume and the placing of instruments. A beginner can first master the basic rhythm patterns and the way of holding the sticks, then practise the division of roles among drums of different sizes; in the theatrical tradition the patterns are classified by tempo, accent, dynamics, pitch and function, and joined into progressions.
長胴太鼓起源於日本，是日本傳統打擊樂器中最具代表性的鼓類樂器。其名稱源於其獨特的: The nagado-daiko originates in Japan and is the most representative drum among Japanese traditional percussion instruments. Its name comes from its distinctive long, cylindrical body. The drum's development can be traced back to ancient Japan, where the influence of Chinese drum culture gradually turned it into an instrument with Japanese character.
長胴太鼓音色雄渾有力，具有深沉而富有穿透力的特質。其音色兼具明亮與暗沉的特色，敲: The nagado-daiko's timbre is powerful and deep, with a penetrating quality. It is both bright and dark: struck at the centre of the head the tone is bright and clear, while at the rim it gives a deep, low resonance. The instrument's range is broad, the low notes full and strong, the high notes crisp and prominent, with good dynamic contrast. Its resonance is distinctive: the cylindrical body and the two heads form a natural resonating chamber, so the sound rings out and spreads fully. Beside the lightness of a snare drum it sounds more dignified, and beside a bass drum it keeps more layers of timbre and expression. Its strong sound pressure and penetration give it a powerful presence in an ensemble, and it is an indispensable core instrument of the traditional Japanese ensemble.
長胴太鼓鼓身採用楸木、桂木或櫸木等優質木材製成，具有良好的共鳴性能。兩面鼓皮使用: The nagado-daiko's body is made from good timber such as catalpa, katsura or zelkova, which resonates well. The two heads are of cowhide or horsehide, carefully prepared for the best tone. The heads are fixed to the two ends of the body with a rope or a metal ring system. The sticks are usually of wood, with leather or cloth wrapped around the tips. The whole instrument is precisely built, each part assembled with care by traditional craft.

It is made of a body and drumheads, and the player strikes the head with sticks to make it sound.
